name: What is the difference between pool resurfacing and pool remodeling?

mainEntity.name: When does resurfacing stop being the right term and become a remodel or renovation instead?
mainEntity.text: When does resurfacing stop being the right term and become a remodel or renovation instead?

acceptedAnswer.text: Resurfacing is a narrower project focused on the pool’s interior skin. Remodeling is broader and can include tile, coping, decking, plumbing, lighting, features, and sometimes even shape changes or equipment upgrades. Homeowners often use the terms loosely, but contractors price them very differently. If the pool only needs a new finish, resurfacing is usually the right category. If several visible or mechanical systems are aging at once, a remodel may be more cost-effective because the work can be coordinated in one project. In the Los Angeles area, many older pools end up in the gray zone between the two because the finish is failing while the tile and coping are also due for replacement. The key is to define the scope first so the estimate reflects what is actually being built.
acceptedAnswer.description: Pool resurfacing means replacing the interior finish only, while pool remodeling usually includes additional work like tile, coping, decking, equipment, lighting, or layout changes. If the job changes the pool beyond the surface layer, it is a remodel. The difference matters because scope, cost, and timeline change quickly.
